macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: U.S. inflation cooled to 3.4% in July, reinforcing expectations the Fed will hold rates steady
items.summary: The latest U.S. CPI report showed headline inflation slowing to 3.4% year over year and core inflation easing to 2.5%, both in line with forecasts. Market coverage said the data bolstered expectations that the Federal Reserve will keep interest rates unchanged at its upcoming meeting.

items.title: Wall Street fell after the Fed kept rates unchanged
items.summary: NBC News reported that Wall Street closed sharply lower after the Federal Reserve left interest rates unchanged. The move kept attention on the central bank's next steps as investors weighed inflation and labor-market signals.

items.title: U.S. stock indexes were mixed to lower in recent trading
items.summary: Recent market snapshots showed the Dow down 60.95 points, the S&P 500 down 4.53 points, and the Nasdaq down 85.26 points. Another market update showed all three major indexes near flat earlier in the session, highlighting a cautious trading tone.

items.title: Strong July labor data and soft ADP hiring kept recession and Fed debates in focus
items.summary: Coverage highlighted an unexpectedly weak U.S. labor backdrop, including a 23,000-job loss in July and ADP's report of just 44,000 private-sector jobs added. The unemployment rate also moved to 4.1%, adding to concerns about a cooling labor market.

items.title: Treasury yields and the dollar were steady ahead of and after U.S. inflation data
items.summary: Reuters-based market coverage said U.S. Treasury yields were largely unchanged after CPI came in as expected, with the 2-year yield around 4.18% and the 10-year near 4.657%. The dollar index was also slightly firmer, reflecting continued focus on Fed policy and geopolitical tensions.

items.title: Asian and European equities traded higher on technology strength and U.S. data anticipation
items.summary: Asian stocks mostly advanced, with renewed strength in technology and semiconductor shares supporting gains in South Korea and Japan. In Europe, the STOXX 600 and major regional indexes were modestly higher as investors awaited U.S. CPI and other macro cues.

items.title: CoreWeave earnings boosted AI-related sentiment in U.S. futures
items.summary: Reuters reported that upbeat results from AI cloud company CoreWeave helped lift U.S. stock futures, especially Nasdaq-linked contracts. The move added to the market's focus on artificial-intelligence beneficiaries in the current earnings season.

items.title: Meta shares fell in extended trading after a higher 2026 capex forecast
items.summary: NBC News said Meta dropped 4% after telling investors it expects 2026 capital expenditures to be higher than previously estimated. The guidance raised fresh questions about spending intensity among large-cap tech companies.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin and major altcoins trade mixed amid cautious risk sentiment
items.summary: Bitcoin slipped about 0.3%-1% over the past 24 hours in several market updates, while Ethereum was slightly higher and XRP hovered near $1.02; traders cited ETF outflows, inflation concerns, and broader macro uncertainty. Litecoin also drew attention after the amount locked in its MWEB feature reached a new all-time high of 505,481.59 LTC.

items.title: SEC set to consider crypto capital-raising rules at August 14 open meeting
items.summary: The U.S. SEC scheduled an open meeting to consider new rules that could let crypto projects raise capital without registering securities, a potentially significant regulatory shift for token issuers. The proposal is being watched as one of the most consequential policy developments in the past day.

items.title: CFTC orders Kalshi to maintain continuous trading operations
items.summary: The U.S. CFTC used emergency authority to require prediction market platform KalshiEX to keep trading continuously, underscoring heightened regulatory scrutiny of event-contract and derivatives platforms. The move adds to a busy day of U.S. regulatory headlines affecting crypto-adjacent markets.

items.title: Russia proposes limited retail crypto trading on regulated exchanges
items.summary: The Bank of Russia reportedly proposed allowing retail crypto trading on regulated exchanges starting September 1, limited to Bitcoin, Ethereum, and USDT. If implemented, it would mark a notable shift in Russia’s long-restrictive approach to retail crypto access.

items.title: MoneyGram launches cash-to-crypto ramps across 170 countries on Solana
items.summary: MoneyGram switched on cash-to-crypto services across 170 countries using Solana infrastructure, expanding real-world crypto payment access. The rollout was highlighted as one of the most important project and adoption developments of the day.

items.title: Coinbase secures Abu Dhabi license for tokenized securities custody
items.summary: Coinbase reportedly received a major license in Abu Dhabi to custody tokenized securities, strengthening its Middle East expansion. The development is part of a broader institutional and regulatory buildout in crypto markets.

items.title: Harmony token plunges after unauthorized mint of roughly 4 billion ONE
items.summary: Harmony confirmed an exploit in which an attacker minted about 4 billion ONE tokens without authorization, sending the token down about 37% to around $0.00077. The incident was one of the sharpest project-specific price moves in the past 24 hours.

items.title: Crypto futures liquidations top $86 million in 24 hours
items.summary: Crypto futures liquidations exceeded $86 million over the last day, reflecting continued volatility in leveraged trading. Liquidation pressure appeared to coincide with choppy price action across major assets.

items.title: BNB and several sector tokens outperform in a narrow crypto market
items.summary: Market data showed crypto trading in a narrow range, with BNB rising about 3.1% and several sector tokens such as DOGE and TWT also posting gains. The report suggests selective strength even as Bitcoin and Ethereum stayed relatively subdued.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: Google says Gemini has surpassed 1 billion monthly users
items.summary: CEO Sundar Pichai said Gemini crossed the 1 billion monthly user mark, making it Google’s fastest-growing product. The milestone follows a recent reorganization of Google’s AI division.

items.title: OpenAI COO Brad Lightcap reportedly plans to leave the company
items.summary: Reports say OpenAI COO Brad Lightcap is preparing to depart to start something new. The move comes as the company continues expanding product and infrastructure efforts.

items.title: Nvidia lines up more than $500 billion in AI infrastructure financing
items.summary: Nvidia reportedly partnered with major financial firms to mobilize over $500 billion for AI infrastructure. The deal highlights continuing market momentum behind data centers, chips, and AI compute capacity.

items.title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT desktop app for Linux in preview
items.summary: OpenAI released a Linux desktop preview for ChatGPT, extending availability to another major developer platform. The app supports ChatGPT Work, Codex, and related features, though some computer-use functionality remains limited.

items.title: Nvidia releases Nemotron 3.5 Lightning and NeMo Switchyard
items.summary: Nvidia announced Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, an open 30B-parameter MoE model, along with NeMo Switchyard, an open-source model routing library for AI agents. The releases reinforce Nvidia’s push into both model development and agent infrastructure.

items.title: Anthropic plans invisible watermarking for Claude outputs
items.summary: Anthropic said Claude will begin applying invisible watermarks to AI-generated text and images. The change is tied to compliance with European Union transparency requirements.

items.title: Anthropic model reportedly made progress on the Riemann hypothesis
items.summary: An unreleased Anthropic model reportedly achieved significant progress on the Riemann hypothesis by coordinating many sub-agents over an extended run. If confirmed, it would be a notable example of frontier models assisting in advanced mathematics research.

items.title: Researchers report a way to extract hidden reasoning traces from frontier models
items.summary: A new research disclosure says hidden reasoning traces can be extracted from frontier AI models. The report also raised questions about whether some Chinese models may have been trained by distilling U.S. models.

items.title: Spotify to label AI-generated artists and exclude them from recommendations
items.summary: Spotify said it will add AI persona badges to AI-generated artists and keep that music out of editorial and algorithmic recommendations starting in mid-September. The policy is part of a broader industry push to manage synthetic content.

items.title: IBM and Together AI sign $240 million cloud agreement
items.summary: IBM and Together AI announced a $240 million multi-year cloud deal. The agreement reflects continued enterprise demand for AI infrastructure and model hosting capacity.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Xbox CEO says The Elder Scrolls 6 is playable after live Bethesda demo
items.summary: Xbox CEO Asha Sharma said she saw a live playthrough of The Elder Scrolls 6 at Bethesda and described its scale as "incredible," while teasing that the story is even bigger. The comments arrived alongside renewed attention from fans trying to infer a subtitle and amid protests over layoffs at Bethesda.

items.title: Quake gets a new free expansion
items.summary: A new free expansion for Quake has been released, adding fresh content to id Software's classic shooter. The update is one of the most notable retro-game announcements in the past day.

items.title: Minecraft launches on Switch 2 in October
items.summary: Minecraft is set to launch on Nintendo Switch 2 on October 27. The announcement adds one of gaming’s biggest titles to Nintendo’s new console lineup.

items.title: Epic Games is offloading ArtStation and Sketchfab
items.summary: Epic Games announced it will transfer ArtStation and Sketchfab to Kitbash, a company that sells 3D assets for games. The move marks another major restructuring of Epic’s creator-focused portfolio.

items.title: Steam hardware shipper breach may have exposed customer data
items.summary: Valve said customer data was "likely compromised" in a breach involving a Steam hardware shipper. The exposed information reportedly includes names and addresses.

items.title: Microsoft begins age verification push for Australian Xbox and PC users
items.summary: Xbox and PC gamers in Australia are reportedly being notified that they will soon need to verify their age before buying 18+ rated apps and games on the Xbox Store and Microsoft Store. The change reflects a broader compliance shift around age-gated content.

items.title: Take-Two says GTA 6 preorders are off to an 'exceptional' start
items.summary: Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick said Grand Theft Auto 6 preorders have had an "unprecedented and astonishing" start during the company’s earnings call. The company also reiterated the game’s release timing.

items.title: Xbox Insider update adds chat-audio controls for captures
items.summary: Xbox Insiders will soon be able to choose whether game chat and party chat audio are included in their captures. The feature gives players more control over what is recorded.

items.title: EA acquisition is officially completed
items.summary: Electronic Arts’ acquisition by Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund, Silver Lake, and Affinity has reportedly been finalized. EA is now a private company and trading in its shares has stopped.

items.title: Xbox Game Pass August 2026 lineup announced
items.summary: Microsoft reportedly revealed the August 2026 Xbox Game Pass lineup, including early access to the Gears of War: E-Day open beta and additions such as PowerWash Simulator 2, Grounded 2, Ball x Pit, and Mio.

items.title: Nexon launches Overwatch in Korea
items.summary: Nexon began domestic service of Blizzard’s Overwatch in South Korea on August 12. The launch marks a notable regional publishing development for the long-running shooter.

tech_news.query: What are the most important technology news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major product launches, company news, and significant tech industry developments. Exclude AI-specific news.

items.title: Intel plans larger stock sale to fund manufacturing expansion
items.summary: Intel said it will increase its planned common stock offering from $15 billion to $20 billion, with proceeds aimed at capital expenditures and expanding its manufacturing footprint. The move comes as the company seeks to meet strong demand for its CPUs.

items.title: Nvidia unveils new open-weights model and routing library
items.summary: Nvidia announced Nemotron 3.5 Lighting, a 30-billion-parameter open-weights model that can run on PCs and data center systems. The company also debuted NeMo Switchyard, an open-source model routing library.

items.title: Nvidia and major asset managers launch $500 billion compute financing push
items.summary: Nvidia said it is partnering with six major U.S. asset managers to raise up to $500 billion to finance AI infrastructure buildout. The effort is designed to help customers fund purchases of Nvidia-powered computing systems.

items.title: Google unveils new Pixel phones with slimmer cameras and added features
items.summary: Google introduced its latest Pixel phones, highlighting slimmer camera hardware and new feature updates. The launch is one of the day’s major consumer-device announcements.

items.title: Spotify to label AI-generated artists and remove them from playlists
items.summary: Spotify said it will begin labeling AI-generated artists and remove them from playlists. The change is intended to increase transparency around synthetic music on the platform.

items.title: Meta unveils new open-source model strategy
items.summary: Meta announced an open-source version of one of its most capable models, intensifying debate over how frontier models should be shared and controlled. The release underscores the company’s broader shift in product strategy.

items.title: Facebook rolls out redesigned Creator Studio
items.summary: Facebook is introducing a reimagined Creator Studio for content creators. The update is part of the platform’s broader product refresh effort.

items.title: France bans unsolicited telemarketing calls
items.summary: France has moved to ban unsolicited telemarketing calls, marking a notable policy development affecting the tech-enabled call and advertising ecosystem. The change could reshape how companies conduct outbound marketing.
